chunks: She was invited to enter the court. When she saw it, she took it for a sheet of water, and (pulling up her skirts) uncovered her legs. (Solomon) told her: "This is paved with tiles of glass." "O Lord," she said, "I have wronged myself, and I submit to the Lord of all the worlds with Solomon."

key_terms.الصَّرْح: Palace or court with a high ceiling

ai.seo_question: What happened when Queen Bilqis visited Prophet Solomon's court and saw the glass floor?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, Bilqis’s act of uncovering her legs is interpreted not merely as a reaction to the glass floor, but as a symbolic shedding of worldly vanity and royal pride before the divine wisdom of Solomon. Her declaration, 'I have wronged myself,' reflects the concept of *al-zulm* (self-injustice) through ignorance, marking her transition from polytheism to monotheism under the guidance of a prophet. This moment underscores the Shia emphasis on the interplay between intellectual recognition of truth and the humble submission of the will to God.
